cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Brighter Side
cards.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said strike with such confidence, so I've made a protest sign. Even with our show cancelled, we'll make ourselves heard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Strike means take down the scenery. Nobody's protesting for us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, take it down together. A splendid chance to get the whole company working side by side!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The company has gone home. It's just us and these flats.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful, we can make every decision ourselves. You choose which flat comes down first; I'll follow your lead. No committee at last!

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies strike as protest and A3 adopts corrected teardown meaning without admitting confusion; A5 makes loss of all helpers an even larger freedom.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 no protest/teardown becomes teamwork opportunity; B4 company gone becomes two-person decision freedom and B-led start.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 want scenery removed and clarify actual labor available.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 reduced workforce as increased agency while still needing B's confident lead.

specificity.evidence: A1 cancelled show and B2 scenery make theatre strike clear; B4 flats are stated scenery pieces.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 choose-first/follow gives B a practical response, though committee tag is a small extra flourish.
